answer.rationale: The 18% cost mandate and 14-day renewal deadline create urgency, but the 94% capacity utilization (no buffer) makes delivery risk the binding constraint. memory_c6 shows multi-year commitments unlock volume pricing without narrowing scope—this is directly applicable. memory_c4 demonstrates that benchmarking recovered margin at renewal. Together, these suggest the incumbent can move on price if presented with a longer commitment. memory_c2 warns that the low-cost vendor is unsuitable as sole source for critical lines, eliminating switch_primary_vendor. Adding a second source (memory_c3) would help resilience but consumes the single decision slot and doesn't address the cost mandate. Deferring risks auto-expiration and month-to-month terms losing leverage. Negotiate_terms targets both cost reduction (via multi-year commitment for volume pricing) and delivery stability (via incumbent relationship continuity), while preserving optionality if negotiation fails. The 18% target may not be fully achievable this cycle, creating downstream risk that must be tracked.
